title: A green, versatile, and facile strategy for anti-biofouling surface with ultra-high graft density polyethylene glycol

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The protocol states "The pH was then adjusted to 5.5 with 0.1 M sodium hydroxide", but the same paragraph later states "All the pH adjustments mentioned above were made using 1 mM salt. Specifically, 1 mM hydrochloric acid and 1 mM sodium hydroxide were used for the above pH adjustments." A 100-fold discrepancy in titrant concentration for the same step makes the deposition protocol irreproducible.

The same mixing step is described twice with contradictory parameters: "shaken on the shaking table (at 800 rpm) for 30 s. Following this, the wafer was left to stand for 10 min. Following 30 s shaking period (at 200 rpm) and a 10-minute resting period...". The agitation speed cannot be both 800 rpm and 200 rpm for the same 30 s/10 min cycle.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction (paragraph on GF vs GT grafting densities)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text argues that GT inherently limits grafting density while "GF is a bottom-up approach, which in principle makes it easier to achieve high-density grafted brush layers", yet immediately reports "The reported maximum grafting density of PEG was 0.79 chains/nm² and 1.9 chains/nm² for the GF and GT strategy, respectively" — i.e., the GT value is higher than GF, directly contradicting the preceding rationale (values appear swapped or misattributed to refs [12, 23]).

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, in vivo/ex vivo thrombosis (rabbit AV shunt) section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Anaesthesia is described twice and inconsistently: first "anaesthetised with sodium pentobarbital at a concentration of 30 mg/ml and a dose of 1 ml/kg", then at the end "The rabbits were anaesthetized using gas and subsequently euthanized by cervical dislocation." Two mutually exclusive anaesthesia protocols are reported for the same animals, and cervical dislocation is not an accepted euthanasia route for rabbits of this size.

"As the probe approaches the coating, it experiences attractive forces. Upon contact with the coating, these attractive forces transform into repulsive forces, and the measured force corresponds to the adhesion energy of the coating." Adhesion (pull-off) force/energy is obtained from the retraction branch of the force–separation curve, not from the approach/contact repulsion; the described measurement does not yield adhesion energy.

The equation is written δ = ρSΔL N_A/(M S); the grafted area S appears in both numerator and denominator and cancels, so its inclusion is meaningless/incorrect as written (the standard expression is δ = ρΔL N_A/M). The symbol list also defines S twice (as grafted area) without any distinct role.

"Hemolysis ratio (%) = (OD samples – OD negative)/(OD positive – OD negative)" yields a dimensionless fraction, not a percentage; the required ×100 factor is missing, so reported hemolysis percentages cannot be reproduced from the stated equation.

The measurement is said to use "the KRUSS DSA1 1.80 version contact angle analyzer" but the data are analysed with "OneAttension software", which is the control/analysis software of Biolin Scientific (Attension) instruments and is not compatible with a KRÜSS DSA system; the instrumentation description is internally inconsistent.

The strains are defined as "Escherichia coli (DH5α) and Staphylococcus aureus (SH1000)", but the protocol then refers to "E. coli and S. aureus epidermidis", conflating two distinct species (S. aureus and S. epidermidis); the organism actually tested is therefore ambiguous.
